prompt: What does Function.compose() do vs Function.andThen()?
choices: compose() runs the function before the other; andThen() runs after — they produce the same result
compose(g) = g runs first, then this function; andThen(g) = this function runs first, then g
compose() is synchronous; andThen() is asynchronous
They are identical methods — one is just an alias for the other
explanation: f.andThen(g).apply(x) = g(f(x)) — f first, then g. f.compose(g).apply(x) = f(g(x)) — g first, then f. Think: andThen = pipeline order, compose = math function composition order.
